text:
One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume $V$ to $2V$ isothermally at a temperature $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ and does $W$ joule of work. If the gas undergoes same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ doing the same amount of work $W$, then its final temperature will be (close to) $____$ ${}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$.

$(\log _{e}2=0.693)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Case -1 : Isothermal Expansion $(\Delta \mathrm{T}=0)$

For an ideal gas undergoing isothermal expansion from $V_{1}$ to $V_{2}$ :

$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{iso}}=\mathrm{nRT}\ln \left (\frac{\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{V}_{1}}\right )$

Given :

$\mathrm{n}=1$ mole

$\mathrm{T}=27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=300\mathrm{K}$

$\frac{\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{V}_{1}}=\frac{2\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}=2$

$\ln 2=0.693$

$W=1\times R\times 300\times 0.693=207.9R$

Case - 2 : Adiabatic Expansion ( $\Delta \mathrm{Q}=0$ )

For an adiabatic process, the work done is given by:

$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{adia}}=\frac{\mathrm{nR}(\mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{T}_{2})}{γ-1}$

The gas is diatomic, so the adiabatic constant $γ=\frac{7}{5}=1.4$.

$\mathrm{T}_{1}=300\mathrm{K}$

Work done is the same magnitude ( $\mathrm{W}=207.9\mathrm{R}$ ).

$207.9\mathrm{R}=\frac{1\times \mathrm{R}(300-\mathrm{T}_{2})}{1.4-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $207.9=\frac{300-\mathrm{T}_{2}}{0.4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $83.16=300-\mathrm{T}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{2}=216.84\mathrm{K}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}({}^{\circ }\mathrm{C})=216.84-273.15$

$\mathrm{T}({}^{\circ }\mathrm{C})\approx -56.31^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

The final temperature is approximately $-56^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A block is sliding down with constant velocity on an inclined plane of slope $θ$ and at an instant $t=0$ this block is given an upward momentum so that it starts moving up on the inclined surface with velocity $u$. The distance $(S)$ travelled by the block before its velocity become zero, is $____$ .

(g = gravitational acceleration)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Before $t=0$ the block slides down the incline with uniform velocity, so kinetic friction balances the component of gravity along the incline:

$μmg\cos θ=mg\sin θ\Rightarrow μ=\tan θ$

While the block moves up, gravity and friction both act down the incline, giving a retardation

$a=g\sin θ+μg\cos θ=2g\sin θ$

The velocity becomes zero after a distance

$S=\dfrac{u^{2}}{2a}=\dfrac{u^{2}}{4g\sin θ}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is 3nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of $17\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by suppling 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, then the piston will move $____$ cm.

(atmospheric pressure $=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the first law of thermodynamics,

$\Delta Q=\Delta U+\Delta W$

Where,

The heat supplied to a system $=\Delta \mathrm{Q}=126\mathrm{J}$

The change in internal energy $=\Delta U=3nRT$

The work done by the system $=\Delta \mathrm{W}$

Number of moles $n=1$ mole of Helium.

Change in temperature $=\Delta \mathrm{T}=4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=4\mathrm{K}$

Since the piston is light, movable, and frictionless, the gas pressure remains equal to the atmospheric pressure $=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$.

Area $=\mathrm{A}=17\mathrm{cm}^{2}=17\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Using the formula provided :

$\Delta \mathrm{U}=3\cdot \mathrm{n}\cdot \mathrm{R}\cdot \Delta \mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{U}=3\cdot 1\cdot 8.314\cdot 4\mathrm{J}$

$\Delta \mathrm{U}=99.768\mathrm{J}$

From the first law :

$\Delta \mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{Q}-\Delta \mathrm{U}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{W}=126-99.768=26.232\mathrm{J}$


[IMG]


Work done by a gas at constant pressure is :

$\Delta \mathrm{W}=\mathrm{P}\Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{P}\times (\mathrm{Ax})$

Where x is the distance the piston moves.

$26.232=10^{5}\times \left (17\times 10^{-4}\right )\times \mathrm{x}$

$\Rightarrow$ $26.232=170\times x$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\frac{26.232}{170}\approx 0.1543\mathrm{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{x}=0.1543\times 100\mathrm{cm}\approx 15.5\mathrm{cm}$

text:
Two short dipoles $(A,B),A$ having charges $\pm 2μ\mathrm{C}$ and length 1 cm and $B$ having charges $\pm 4μ\mathrm{C}$ and length 1 cm are placed with their centres 80 cm apart as shown in the figure. The electric field at a point $P$, equi-distant from the centres of both dipoles is $____$ N/C.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The dipole moment is given by $\mathrm{p}=\mathrm{q}\times 2\mathrm{l}$.

For Dipole A : $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{A}}=2\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{C},2\mathrm{l}=1\mathrm{cm}=0.01\mathrm{m}$.

$\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{A}}=\left (2\times 10^{-6}\right )(0.01)=2\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{C}\cdot \mathrm{m}$

For Dipole B : $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{B}}=4\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{C},2\mathrm{l}=1\mathrm{cm}=0.01\mathrm{m}$.

$p_{B}=\left (4\times 10^{-6}\right )(0.01)=4\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{C}\cdot \mathrm{m}$

The distance between the centres is 80 cm .

Point P is equi-distant from both, so it is at the midpoint : $\mathrm{r}=40\mathrm{cm}=0.4\mathrm{m}$.

Point P is on the axial line of dipole A and on the equatorial line of dipole B .

Field due to A (Axial) :

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{2\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{r}^{3}}=\frac{\left (9\times 10^{9}\right )2\left (2\times 10^{-8}\right )}{(0.4)^{3}}=\frac{360}{0.064}=5625\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}$

It is along the axis of dipole A (horizontal)

Field due to B (Equatorial) :

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\frac{\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{r}^{3}}=\frac{\left (9\times 10^{9}\right )4\times 10^{-8}}{(0.4)^{3}}=\frac{360}{0.064}=5625\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}$

It acts opposite to the direction of dipole B (vertical).

Since the vectors are perpendicular and equal in magnitude $(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{E})$ :

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{net}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}+\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}^{2}}=\mathrm{E}\sqrt{2}$

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{net}}=5625\sqrt{2}\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{C}}=0.5625\sqrt{2}\times 10^{4}=\frac{9}{16}\sqrt{2}\times 10^{4}\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{C}}$

So, net electric field at point P is, $\mathrm{E}_{\text{net}}=\frac{9}{16}\sqrt{2}\times 10^{4}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A circular loop of radius 7 cm is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T directed perpendicular to plane of loop. The loop is converted into a square loop in 0.5 s . The EMF induced in the loop is $____$ mV.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, the induced EMF (E) is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux $(𝜙)$ through the loop.

Initially circular loop is with radius $\mathrm{r}=7\mathrm{cm}=0.07\mathrm{m}$.

Finally a square loop formed from the same wire.

Magnetic field $\mathrm{B}=0.2\mathrm{T}$ (constant and perpendicular).

Time interval $=\Delta \mathrm{t}=0.5\mathrm{s}$.

Initial Area ( $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ )

$\mathrm{A}_{1}=π\mathrm{r}^{2}=π\times (0.07)^{2}=0.0154\mathrm{m}^{2}$

The perimeter of the square must be equal to the circumference of the circle because the wire length is constant.

$2π\mathrm{r}=4\mathrm{a}\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{2π\mathrm{r}}{4}=\frac{π\mathrm{r}}{2}=\frac{π\times 0.07}{2}\mathrm{m}=0.11\mathrm{m}$

So, final area ( $\mathrm{A}_{2}$ )

$a^{2}=(0.11)^{2}=0.0121m^{2}.$

Since the field is perpendicular, $𝜙=\mathrm{B}\cdot \mathrm{A}$.

So, the change in magnetic flux is,

$\Delta 𝜙=\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{A}_{2}-\mathrm{A}_{1})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta 𝜙=0.2\times (0.0121-0.0154)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta 𝜙=0.2\times (-0.0033)=-0.00066\mathrm{Wb}$

The magnitude of the induced EMF is :

$|E|=\left |\frac{\Delta 𝜙}{\Delta t}\right |$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\mathrm{E}|=\frac{0.00066}{0.5}=0.00132\mathrm{V}=0.00132\times 1000\mathrm{mV}=1.32\mathrm{mV}$

Therefore, the induced EMF is 1.32 mV . 

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
A bead $P$ sliding on a frictionless semi-circular string $(ACB)$ and it is at point $S$ at $t=0$ and at this instant the horizontal component of its velocity is $v$. Another bead $Q$ of the same mass as $P$ is ejected from point $A$ at $t=0$ along the horizontal string $AB$, with the speed $v$, friction between the beads and the respective strings may be neglected in both cases. Let $t_{P}$ and $t_{Q}$ be the respective times taken by beads $P$ and $Q$ to reach the point $B$, then the relation between $t_{P}$ and $t_{Q}$ is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Taking the semicircular string in a horizontal plane (no value of $g$ or $R$ enters the data), the only force on P along its path is the normal reaction of the string, which is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work, so P moves with constant speed.

At S the tangent to the circle makes $45^{\circ }$ with AB, so the speed of P is

$u=\dfrac{v}{\cos 45^{\circ }}=\sqrt{2}v$

The arc from S through C to B subtends $180^{\circ }-45^{\circ }=135^{\circ }$ at the centre, so its length is $\dfrac{3πR}{4}$ and

$t_{P}=\dfrac{3πR/4}{\sqrt{2}v}=\dfrac{3πR}{4\sqrt{2}v}\approx 1.67\dfrac{R}{v}$

Q moves along AB, of length $2R$, with constant speed $v$: $t_{Q}=\dfrac{2R}{v}$.

So $\dfrac{t_{P}}{t_{Q}}=\dfrac{3π}{8\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.83$, and $t_{P}<t_{Q}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2 s of free fall and starts decelerating with $3\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. At 10 m height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is $5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The initial height of the airplane is $____$ m.

$\left (\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Interval 1 : Free Fall (Before opening the parachute)

The paratrooper is falling under gravity with $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ starting from rest ( $\mathrm{u}_{1}=0$ ).

$\text{Time}=\mathrm{t}_{1}=2\mathrm{s}$

Using equation of motion, the distance covered is

$\mathrm{h}_{1}=\mathrm{u}_{1}\mathrm{t}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{gt}_{1}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow\mathrm{h}_{1}=0+\frac{1}{2}(10)(2)^{2}=20\mathrm{m}$

Let the velocity at the end of interval 1 is $v_{1}$

$\mathrm{v}_{1}=\mathrm{u}_{1}+\mathrm{gt}_{1}=0+(10)(2)=20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Interval 2 : Deceleration (After opening the parachute)

The parachute opens, and the paratrooper starts decelerating until reaching a height of 10 m above the ground.

Initial velocity for this interval $=\mathrm{u}_{2}=20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ (velocity $\mathrm{v}_{1}$ from interval 1)

Final velocity $=\mathrm{v}_{2}=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Acceleration $\mathrm{a}=-3\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ (deceleration)

So, the distance covered in interval 2, using the third equation of motion :

$\mathrm{v}_{2}^{2}=\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}+2\mathrm{ah}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(5)^{2}=(20)^{2}+2(-3)\mathrm{h}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $25=400-6\mathrm{h}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{h}_{2}=\frac{375}{6}=62.5\mathrm{m}$

The total initial height,

$\mathrm{H}=\mathrm{h}_{1}+\mathrm{h}_{2}+\mathrm{h}_{\text{ground}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{H}=20+62.5+10$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{H}=92.5\mathrm{m}$

So, the airplane was at a height of 92.5 m when the paratrooper jumped. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant $k=3$ and permeability of $μ=2μ_{0}$, is ( $μ_{0}=$ permeability of vacuum)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The speed of light (or any electromagnetic wave) in a vacuum is given by the formula :

$c=\frac{1}{\sqrt{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}}$

Where :

1. $μ_{0}$ is the permeability of free space.

2. $𝜖_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space.

The speed of light in a specific medium is determined by that medium's permeability ( $μ$ ) and permittivity ( $𝜖$ ):

$v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{μ𝜖}}$

For the given medium :

Permeability : $μ=2μ_{0}$

Dielectric Constant $\mathrm{k}=3$. The dielectric constant (relative permittivity $𝜖_{\mathrm{r}}$ ) is defined as $𝜖_{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{𝜖}{𝜖_{0}}$. Therefore, $𝜖=\mathrm{k}𝜖_{0}=3𝜖_{0}$.

We need to find the ratio $c:v$, which is the same as the refractive index $n$ of the medium.

$\frac{c}{v}=\frac{1/\sqrt{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}}{1/\sqrt{μ𝜖}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{c}{v}=\sqrt{\frac{μ𝜖}{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}}=\sqrt{\frac{(2μ_{0})(3𝜖_{0})}{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}}$

For the medium $μ=2μ_{0}$ and $𝜖=3𝜖_{0}$ :

$\frac{c}{v}=\sqrt{\frac{(2μ_{0})(3𝜖_{0})}{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{1}$

The ratio of the speed in vacuum to the speed in the medium is $\sqrt{6}:1$. 

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Suppose a long solenoid of 100 cm length, radius 2 cm having 500 turns per unit length, carries a current $I=10\sin (ω\mathrm{t})\mathrm{A}$, where $ω=1000\mathrm{rad}./\mathrm{s}$. A circular conducting loop $(B)$ of radius 1 cm coaxially slided through the solenoid at a speed $v=1\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. The r.m.s. current through the loop when the coil $B$ is inserted 10 cm inside the solenoid is $\frac{α}{\sqrt{2}}μA$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

[Resistance of the loop $=10\Omega$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Inside a long solenoid the field is uniform, $B=μ_{0}nI$, with $n=500\text{m}^{-1}$ and $I=10\sin (1000t)\text{A}$.


[IMG]

At 10 cm inside the 100 cm solenoid the coaxial loop (radius $r=1\text{cm}=0.01\text{m}$) lies in this uniform field, so its motion along the axis does not change the flux; only the changing current does:

$\Phi =μ_{0}nIπr^{2}=μ_{0}nπr^{2}\times 10\sin (1000t)$

$|ε|=\dfrac{d\Phi }{dt}=μ_{0}nπr^{2}\times 10\times 1000\cos (1000t)$

Peak current with $R=10\Omega$:

$i_{0}=\dfrac{(4π\times 10^{-7})(500)(π\times 10^{-4})(10^{4})}{10}=2π^{2}\times 10^{-5}\text{A}\approx 1.97\times 10^{-4}\text{A}=197μ\text{A}$

$i_{\text{rms}}=\dfrac{i_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{197}{\sqrt{2}}μ\text{A}\Rightarrow α=197$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio $2:2:3$. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of $18\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is

$____$ $\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The masses are in the ratio $2:2:3$ with a total of 14 kg, so $7x=14\Rightarrow x=2$ and the fragments are 4 kg, 4 kg and 6 kg.

The body is initially at rest, so the total momentum after the explosion is zero: $⃗{p}_{3}=-\left (⃗{p}_{1}+⃗{p}_{2}\right )$.


[IMG]

The two 4 kg fragments move perpendicular to each other, each with momentum $4\times 18=72\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, so

$\left |⃗{p}_{1}+⃗{p}_{2}\right |=\sqrt{72^{2}+72^{2}}=72\sqrt{2}\text{kg m s}^{-1}$

For the 6 kg fragment,

$v_{3}=\dfrac{72\sqrt{2}}{6}=12\sqrt{2}\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws $25%$ more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initially, the capacitor has air between the plates with separation $\mathrm{d}=5\mathrm{mm}=5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$.

The initial capacitance ( $\mathrm{C}_{0}$ ) is:

$C_{0}=\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{d}=\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{5}$

Where A is the area of the plates and d is in mm ).

A mica sheet of thickness $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{mm}$ and dielectric constant K is introduced. The new capacitance $(\mathrm{C}^{'})$ of a capacitor partially filled with a dielectric is given by:

$C^{'}=\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{d-t+\frac{t}{K}}$

Substituting the values $\mathrm{d}=5$ and $\mathrm{t}=2$ :

$C^{'}=\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{5-2+\frac{2}{K}}=\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{3+\frac{2}{K}}$

The battery remains connected, meaning the potential difference (V) stays constant.

Initial charge: $\mathrm{Q}_{0}=\mathrm{C}_{0}\mathrm{V}$

Final charge: $Q^{'}=C^{'}V$

The capacitor draws $25%$ more charge :

$\mathrm{Q}^{'}=\mathrm{Q}_{0}+0.25\mathrm{Q}_{0}=1.25\mathrm{Q}_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C}^{'}\mathrm{V}=1.25\mathrm{C}_{0}\mathrm{V}$

$\Rightarrow C^{'}=\frac{5}{4}C_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{𝜖_{0}\mathrm{A}}{3+\frac{2}{\mathrm{K}}}=\frac{5}{4}\left (\frac{𝜖_{0}\mathrm{A}}{5}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{3+\frac{2}{K}}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3+\frac{2}{K}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2}{\mathrm{K}}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $K=2$

The dielectric constant K is 2.0 . 

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Atoms are represented by the notation $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{Z}}^{\mathrm{A}}$, where :

1. A is the Mass Number (total number of protons and neutrons).

2. $\mathrm{Z}$ is the Atomic Number (number of protons).

Isobars are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same mass number (A) but different atomic numbers (Z).

Option A : $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{3}$ and $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{3}$

Mass numbers: 3 and 3 (Same)

Atomic numbers: 1 and 2 (Different)

Since they have the same mass number ( $A=3$ ) but represent different elements ( $Z=1$ vs $Z=2$ ), they are Isobars. Hence, option (A) is correct.

Option B : $\mathrm{Hg}_{80}^{198}$ and $\mathrm{Au}_{79}^{197}$

Mass numbers: 198 and 197 (Different)

Atomic numbers: 80 and 79 (Different)

So, $\mathrm{Hg}_{80}^{198}$ and $\mathrm{Au}_{79}^{197}$ are neither isobars nor isotopes. Hence, option (B) is incorrect.

Option C : $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{3}$

Mass numbers: 2 and 3 (Different)

Atomic numbers: 1 and 1 (Same)

So, $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{3}$ are Isotopes of Hydrogen (Deuterium and Tritium). Hence, option (C) is incorrect.

Option D : $\mathrm{U}_{92}^{236}$ and $\mathrm{U}_{92}^{238}$

Mass numbers: 236 and 238 (Different)

Atomic numbers: 92 and 92 (Same)

So, $\mathrm{U}_{92}^{236}$ and $\mathrm{U}_{92}^{238}$ are Isotopes (same element, different mass) not isobars. Hence, option (D) is incorrect.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: To compare EMF of two cells using potentiometer the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm . The least count of scale is 1 cm . The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The EMF (E) of a cell in a potentiometer is directly proportional to its balancing length (l).


[IMG]


Therefore, the ratio of the EMFs of two cells is given by :

$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{E}_{1}}{\mathrm{E}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_{1}}{\mathrm{l}_{2}}$

Balancing length for first cell $\mathrm{l}_{1}=200\mathrm{cm}$

Balancing length for second cell $\mathrm{l}_{2}=150\mathrm{cm}$

Absolute error in measurement $\Delta \mathrm{l}_{1}=\Delta \mathrm{l}_{2}=1\mathrm{cm}$ (the least count of the scale)

For a ratio $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_{1}}{\mathrm{l}_{2}}$, the relative error $\left (\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}}\right )$ is the sum of the relative errors of the individual components :

$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_{1}}{\mathrm{l}_{1}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_{2}}{\mathrm{l}_{2}}$

Percentage Error $=\left (\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_{1}}{\mathrm{l}_{1}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_{2}}{\mathrm{l}_{2}}\right )\times 100=\left (\frac{1}{200}+\frac{1}{150}\right )\times 100\approx 1.17%$

The calculated percentage error is approximately $1.17%$.

text: Two charges $7μ\mathrm{C}$ and $-2μ\mathrm{C}$ are placed at $(-9,0,0)\mathrm{cm}$ and $(9,0,0)\mathrm{cm}$ respectively in an external field $E=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{r^{2}}\hat{r}$, where $A=9\times 10^{5}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}.\mathrm{m}^{2}$. Considering the potential at infinity is 0 , the electrostatic energy of the configuration is $____$ J.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The radial external field $E=\dfrac{A}{r^{2}}$ has potential $V(r)=\dfrac{A}{r}$, taking $V(\infty )=0$.

Both charges are at $r=9\text{cm}=0.09\text{m}$ from the origin, so

$V=\dfrac{9\times 10^{5}}{0.09}=10^{7}\text{V}$

Energy of the two charges in the external field:

$q_{1}V+q_{2}V=(7-2)\times 10^{-6}\times 10^{7}=70-20=50\text{J}$

Mutual interaction energy, with separation $d=18\text{cm}=0.18\text{m}$:

$U_{12}=\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\dfrac{q_{1}q_{2}}{d}=\dfrac{9\times 10^{9}\times (7\times 10^{-6})\times (-2\times 10^{-6})}{0.18}=-0.7\text{J}$

Total electrostatic energy of the configuration:

$U=50-0.7=49.3\text{J}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A prism of angle $75^{\circ }$ and refractive index $\sqrt{3}$ is coated with thin film of refractive index 1.5 only at the back exit surface. To have total internal reflection at the back exit surface the incident angle must be $____$

$(\sin 15^{\circ }=0.25$ and $\sin 25^{\circ }=0.43)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total internal reflection (TIR) occurs at the interface between the prism ( $n_{p}=\sqrt{3}$ ) and the film ( $n_{f}=1.5$ ).

$\sin C=\frac{n_{\text{rarer}}}{n_{\text{denser}}}=\frac{1.5}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow C=\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )=60^{\circ }$

So, the critical angle is $C=60^{\circ }$.

For TIR to occur at the second surface, the angle of incidence $r_{2}$ must satisfy:

$r_{2}>C\Rightarrow r_{2}>60^{\circ }$

For a prism with angle $\mathrm{A}=75^{\circ }$ :

$\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{r}_{1}+\mathrm{r}_{2}\Rightarrow 75^{\circ }=\mathrm{r}_{1}+\mathrm{r}_{2}$

Substituting the condition $\mathrm{r}_{2}>60^{\circ }$ :

$r_{1}=75^{\circ }-r_{2}<75^{\circ }-60^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{r}_{1}<15^{\circ }$

Apply Snell's Law at the first surface (assuming air to prism) :

$\mathrm{n}_{\text{air}}\sin \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{p}}\sin \mathrm{r}_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin \mathrm{i}=\sqrt{3}\sin \mathrm{r}_{1}$

Since $\mathrm{r}_{1}<15^{\circ }$, then $\sin \mathrm{i}<\sqrt{3}\sin 15^{\circ }$ :

$\sin i<1.732\times 0.25$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin i<0.433$

Given that $\sin 25^{\circ }=0.43$, we can conclude:

$\mathrm{i}<25^{\circ }$

For the angle $r_{2}$ to remain above $60^{\circ }$, i.e., the value of $r_{1}$ will be between 0 and $15^{\circ }$. The maximum value of $r_{2}$ can be $75^{\circ }$ for which $\mathrm{r}_{1}=0$.

$\sin \mathrm{i}=\sqrt{3}\sin 0^{\circ }=0$

So, the value of i will be between $0^{\circ }$ and $25^{\circ }$.

text:
The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side $4\sqrt{3}\mathrm{cm}$ is 2 A . The magnetic field at its centroid is $α\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{T}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

(Given : $μ_{\mathrm{o}}=4π\times 10^{-7}$ SI units)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let L be the side of the equilateral triangle, where $\mathrm{L}=4\sqrt{3}\mathrm{cm}=4\sqrt{3}\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$.

The centroid $O$ is equidistant from all three sides. Let $r$ be the perpendicular distance from the centroid to any side.


[IMG]


In an equilateral triangle :

$\tan 60^{\circ }=\sqrt{3}=\frac{L/2}{r}\Rightarrow r=\frac{L}{2\sqrt{3}}$

Substituting the value of L :

$\mathrm{r}=\frac{4\sqrt{3}\times 10^{-2}}{2\sqrt{3}}=2\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

The magnetic field $B_{1}$ due to a straight wire of finite length at a distance $r$ is given by :

$\mathrm{B}_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{4π\mathrm{r}}(\sin θ_{1}+\sin θ_{2})$

Here, $θ_{1}=θ_{2}=60^{\circ }$

$B_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(\sin 60^{\circ }+\sin 60^{\circ })=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(2\sin 60^{\circ })$

$\Rightarrow$ $B_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}\left (2\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )=\frac{μ_{0}I\sqrt{3}}{4πr}$

Since there are three sides and the current flows in a way that all three fields at the centroid point in the same direction,

$B_{net}=3\times B_{1}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}μ_{0}I}{4πr}$

Substituting the given values :

1. $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}$

2. $\mathrm{I}=2\mathrm{A}$

3. $\mathrm{r}=2\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

$\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{net}}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}\times \left (4π\times 10^{-7}\right )\times 2}{4π\times \left (2\times 10^{-2}\right )}\mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{net}}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}\times 10^{-7}\times 2}{2\times 10^{-2}}\mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{net}}=3\sqrt{3}\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{T}=α\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow α=3\sqrt{3}$

For the given logic gate circuit, which of the following is the correct truth table?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Gate I is an OR gate with inputs $n$ and $m$, so its output is $Y_{1}=n+m$.


[IMG]

Gate II is a NAND gate with inputs $n$ and $Y_{1}$:

$z=n\cdot (n+m)–$

By the absorption law, $n\cdot (n+m)=n\cdot n+n\cdot m=n+nm=n(1+m)=n$, so

$z=n–$

The output depends only on $n$: $z=1$ when $n=0$ and $z=0$ when $n=1$, whatever the value of $m$. For example, $n=1,m=0$ gives $Y_{1}=1$ and $z=1\cdot 1–=0$.

For $(n,m)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0)$ the outputs are $z=1,1,0,0$, which is the table in option (A).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A small metallic sphere of diameter 2 mm and density $10.5\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density $1.5\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is $____$ $\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$.

$\left (π=\frac{22}{7} \right.$ and $\left. g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using Stokes' Law, the formula for terminal velocity $(v_{t})$ of a spherical body falling through a viscous fluid is :

$v_{t}=\frac{2r^{2}(ρ-σ)g}{9η}$

Where :

$r=$ Radius of the sphere $r=\frac{\text{Diameter}}{2}=\frac{2\mathrm{mm}}{2}=1\mathrm{mm}=0.1\mathrm{cm}$.

$ρ=$ Density of the sphere $=ρ=10.5\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

$σ=$ Density of the fluid, Density of glycerine $=σ=1.5\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

$\mathrm{g}=$ Acceleration due to gravity $=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}=1000\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

$η=$ Coefficient of viscosity $=10$ Poise

1 Poise $=1\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{cm}\cdot \mathrm{s}^{3}}$, which is the CGS unit of viscosity.

Substituting the values into the terminal velocity equation :

$v_{t}=\frac{2\times (0.1)^{2}\times (10.5-1.5)\times 1000}{9\times 10}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{2\times 0.01\times 9\times 1000}{9\times 10}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}=2\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$

The sphere accelerates until the viscous drag reaches a point where the upward forces equal the weight of the sphere. At this point, it continues to fall at a constant terminal velocity of $2.0\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
An air bubble of volume $2.9\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is $17^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, is $____$ $\mathrm{cm}^{3}$.

( $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, density of water $=10^{3}\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$, and 1 atm pressure is $10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initial state (at the bottom)

Volume $=\mathrm{V}_{1}=2.9\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

Temperature $=\mathrm{T}_{1}=17^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=17+273=290\mathrm{K}$

Pressure $=\mathrm{P}_{1}$

Total pressure at the bottom is atmospheric pressure $(\mathrm{P}_{0})$ plus the hydrostatic pressure $(\mathrm{h}ρ\mathrm{g})$.

$P_{1}=10^{5}+10^{3}\times 10\times 5=1.5\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$

Final state (at the surface)

Temperature $=\mathrm{T}_{2}=27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=27+273=300\mathrm{K}$

Pressure $=P_{2}=P_{0}$ (Only atmospheric pressure acts at the surface.)

$\mathrm{P}_{2}=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$

According to the Ideal Gas Law :

$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}\mathrm{V}_{1}}{\mathrm{T}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{T}_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\left (1.5\times 10^{5}\right )\times 2.9}{290}=\frac{\left (10^{5}\right )\times V_{2}}{300}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1.5\times 2.9}{290}=\frac{V_{2}}{300}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{2}=\frac{1.5\times 2.9\times 300}{290}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{V}_{2}=4.5\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

So, as the bubble rises, the external pressure decreases significantly while the temperature increases slightly. Both factors contribute to the expansion of the air bubble, resulting in a final volume of $4.5\mathrm{cm}^{3}$. 

Therefore, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
When an unpolarized light falls at a particular angle on a glass plate (placed in air), it is observed that the reflected beam is linearly polarized. The angle of refracted beam with respect to the normal is $____$ .

$\left (\tan ^{-1}(1.52)=57.7^{\circ } \right.$, refractive indices of air and glass are 1.00 and 1.52, respectively.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When unpolarized light strikes an interface at a specific angle called the Brewster angle ( $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{B}}$ or $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}$ ), the reflected light is completely linearly polarized. At this specific angle, the reflected ray and the refracted ray are perpendicular $(90^{\circ })$ to each other.


[IMG]


1. $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}=$ Angle of incidence (polarizing angle)

2. $θ_{\mathrm{r}}=$ Angle of reflection

3. $θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=$ Angle of refraction

Since the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence :

$θ_{\mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}$

Since the angle between the reflected and refracted ray is $90^{\circ }$ :

$\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}+90^{\circ }+θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=180^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=90^{\circ }-\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}$

Applying Snell's Law

$μ_{1}\sin (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=μ_{2}\sin (θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}})$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ_{1}\sin (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=μ_{2}\sin (90^{\circ }-\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ_{1}\sin (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=μ_{2}\cos (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\tan (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=\frac{μ_{2}}{μ_{1}}$

If the first medium is air ( $μ_{1}\approx 1$ ), the formula simplifies to :

$\tan (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=μ$

Substituting the values:

$\tan (\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}})=\frac{1.52}{1.00}=1.52$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}=\tan ^{-1}(1.52)=57.7^{\circ }$

As established by the geometry of Brewster's condition :

$\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}+θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=90^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=90^{\circ }-\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{p}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=90^{\circ }-57.7^{\circ }$

$θ_{\mathrm{r}^{'}}=32.3^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ The angle of the refracted beam with respect to the normal is $32.3^{\circ }$. Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The size of the images of an object, formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8 cm and 24 cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is $____$ cm.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a thin lens to form images of the same size at two different object positions, one image must be real and the other must be virtual. This typically occurs with a convex lens.

If the object distance is $u$, focal length of lens is $f$ then lens formula is given as,

$\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}=\frac{u+f}{uf}$

The magnification is given as $m=\frac{v}{u}\Rightarrow m=\frac{1}{u}\times \left [\frac{uf}{u+f}\right ]=\frac{f}{f+u}$

Where:

f is the focal length.

u is the object distance (using sign convention, u is negative).

Since the sizes (magnitudes of magnification) are equal but the nature of the images is different:

$|\mathrm{m}_{1}|=|\mathrm{m}_{2}|\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}_{1}=-\mathrm{m}_{2}$

Given:

1. Position $1=\mathrm{u}_{1}=-8\mathrm{cm}$

2. Position $2=\mathrm{u}_{2}=-24\mathrm{cm}$

$\frac{f}{f+(-8)}=-\left (\frac{f}{f+(-24)}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{f-8}=-\frac{1}{f-24}$

$\Rightarrow$ $f-24=-(f-8)$

$\Rightarrow$ $f-24=-f+8$

$\Rightarrow$ $2\mathrm{f}=32$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{f}=16\mathrm{cm}$

The focal length of the lens that produces images of equal size at object distances of 8 cm and 24 cm is 16 cm. 

Hence, the correct answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of ${}_{92}^{235}\mathrm{U}$ is 190 MeV . When all the atoms of 47 g pure ${}_{92}^{235}\mathrm{U}$ undergo fission process, the energy released is $α\times 10^{23}\mathrm{MeV}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

(Avogadro Number $=6\times 10^{23}$ per mole)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number of moles (n) is given by the formula :

$\mathrm{n}=\frac{\text{Given Mass}}{\text{Molar Mass}}$

Given :

Mass of Uranium $=47\mathrm{g}$

Molar Mass of $\mathrm{U}_{92}^{235}=235\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$

$\mathrm{n}=\frac{47}{235}=\frac{1}{5}=0.2\mathrm{moles}$

Each mole contains a number of atoms equal to Avogadro's Number ( $N_{A}$ ).

$\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{n}\times \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{N}=0.2\times \left (6\times 10^{23}\right )$

Since each atom (nucleus) releases 190 MeV upon fission :

$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{N}\times \text{Energy per fission}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{E}=\left (1.2\times 10^{23}\right )\times 190\mathrm{MeV}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{E}=228\times 10^{23}\mathrm{MeV}$

$\Rightarrow α\times 10^{23}\mathrm{MeV}=228\times 10^{23}\mathrm{MeV}$

$\Rightarrow α=228$

Therefore, the correct answer is $𝟐 𝟐 𝟖$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from $0^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $α{}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The velocity of sound in an ideal gas depends on the absolute temperature of the medium.

The speed of sound (v) in air is given by the formula :

$\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{γ\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}$

From this, we can see that :

$\mathrm{v}\propto \sqrt{\mathrm{T}}$

where T is the absolute temperature in Kelvin $(\mathrm{K})$.

Initial State :

Temperature $=\mathrm{T}_{1}=0^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=(0+273)\mathrm{K}=273\mathrm{K}$

Velocity $=\mathrm{v}_{1}$

Final State :

Temperature $=\mathrm{T}_{2}=α^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=(α+273)\mathrm{K}$

Velocity $=\mathrm{v}_{2}=2\mathrm{v}_{1}($ since the velocity is doubled $)$.

Using the proportionality $\mathrm{v}\propto \sqrt{\mathrm{T}}$ :

$\frac{\mathrm{v}_{2}}{\mathrm{v}_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}_{2}}{\mathrm{T}_{1}}}$

Substituting the values :

$\frac{2v_{1}}{v_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{α+273}{273}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $4=\frac{α+273}{273}$

$\Rightarrow$ $4\times 273=α+273$

$\Rightarrow$ $α=1092-273$

$\Rightarrow$ $α=819$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 819 . Hence, the correct answer is $𝟖 𝟏 𝟗$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass $M\mathrm{kg}$ and radius $r\mathrm{m}$ shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis $A$ of the disc is given by $\frac{x}{256}Mr^{2}$. The value of $x$ is $____$ .


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of full disc is M

Radius of full disc is $r$

Surface Mass Density $=σ=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{π\mathrm{r}^{2}}$

Two identical small discs of radius $r^{'}=\frac{r}{4}$ are removed.

Mass of each small disc (m):

$\mathrm{m}=σ\times π(\mathrm{r}^{'})^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{π\mathrm{r}^{2}}\times π\left (\frac{\mathrm{r}}{4}\right )^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{16}$

The centre of each small disc is at a distance $\mathrm{d}=\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{r}$ from the central point. Since axis A passes through the centre perpendicular to the plane of the disc, the distance of each centre from axis A is $\mathrm{d}=\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{r}$.

The moment of inertia of full disc $\left (\mathrm{I}_{\text{total}}\right )$ :

$\mathrm{I}_{\text{total}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}$

The moment of inertia of small disc about its own centre ( $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ ):

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{r}^{'})^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{\mathrm{M}}{16}\right )\left (\frac{\mathrm{r}}{4}\right )^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{Mr}^{2}}{512}$

The moment of inertia of small disc about axis A ( $\mathrm{I}_{\text{removed}}$ ) using the parallel axis theorem :

$\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{cm}}+\mathrm{md}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{I}_{\text{removed}}=\frac{\mathrm{Mr}^{2}}{512}+\left (\frac{\mathrm{M}}{16}\right )\left (\frac{3\mathrm{r}}{4}\right )^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{Mr}^{2}}{512}+\frac{9\mathrm{Mr}^{2}}{256}=\frac{\mathrm{Mr}^{2}+18\mathrm{Mr}^{2}}{512}=\frac{19}{512}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}$

The moment of inertia of rest of the system is ( $I_{\text{rem}}$ )

$\mathrm{I}_{\text{rem}}=\mathrm{I}_{\text{total}}-2\left (\mathrm{I}_{\text{removed}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $I_{\mathrm{rem}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}-2\left (\frac{19}{512}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}\right )=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}-\frac{19}{256}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rem}}=\left (\frac{128-19}{256}\right )\mathrm{Mr}^{2}=\frac{109}{256}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{256}\mathrm{Mr}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow x=109$

Therefore, the value of x is 109 . Hence, the correct answer is $𝟏 𝟎 𝟗$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: A ball of radius $r$ and density $ρ$ dropped through a viscous liquid of density $σ$ and viscosity $η$ attains its terminal velocity at time $t$, given by $t=Aρ^{a}r^{b}η^{c}σ^{d}$, where $A$ is a constant and $a,b,c$ and $d$ are integers. The value of $\frac{b+c}{a+d}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dimensions of Each Quantity

We first write the dimensions of every symbol in the formula.

Time $[\mathrm{t}]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{1}\right ]$

Density $[ρ]=[σ]=\left [\frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-3}\right ]$

Radius $[\mathrm{r}]=[\mathrm{L}]$

From Stokes' Law ( $F=6πη$ rv), we have $η=$ F/rv.

Using Stokes’ law, $η$ depends on force, radius, and velocity, so its dimensions come from $F$, $r$, and $v$.

Dimension $=\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ][\mathrm{L}^{-1}]\left [\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{T}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$

Constant (A) is dimensionless

According to the given formula $t=Aρ^{a}r^{b}η^{c}σ^{d}$ :

$[\mathrm{T}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-3}\right ]^{\mathrm{a}}[\mathrm{L}]^{\mathrm{b}}\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]^{\mathrm{c}}\left [\mathrm{ML}^{-3}\right ]^{\mathrm{d}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{1}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{d}}\right ]\left [\mathrm{L}^{-3\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c}-3\mathrm{d}}\right ][\mathrm{T}^{-\mathrm{c}}]$

Comparing the exponents for $\mathrm{M},\mathrm{L}$, and T on both sides :

For $\mathrm{T}:-\mathrm{c}=1\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=-1$

For $\mathrm{M}:\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{d}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}-1+\mathrm{d}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}=1$

For $\mathrm{L}:-3\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c}-3\mathrm{d}=0$

Substituting $\mathrm{c}=-1$ :

$-3a+b+1-3d=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $b+1-3(a+d)=0$

Substituting $(a+d)=1$

$b+1-3(1)=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $b-2=0\Rightarrow b=2$

We need to find the value of $\frac{b+c}{a+d}$ :

$\frac{b+c}{a+d}=\frac{2+(-1)}{1}=1$

Therefore, the correct answer is $𝟏$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift
